objective: Define a versioned, backward-compatible Verification manifest and result contract for Cezar Factory while preserving existing validation.changed/full/verify behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a project with only the existing validation.changed/full/verify entries, when the new contract is parsed, then those entries remain valid and are not rewritten. Given a valid version-1 verification manifest, when checks run, then typed run/check results preserve status, diagnostics, metrics, coverage, finding identity, environment, provenance, and bounded artifact references. Given an empty required suite, parser error, unsupported schema version, required skipped or unknown check, tool crash, timeout, cancellation, or truncated evidence, when results aggregate, then the outcome is explicit and never passed. Given equivalent fixture inputs on Windows and Linux, when an independent consumer validates them, then the same status and semantic exit code are observed. Performance policy consumes recorded metrics and does not rerun operations; verification results remain separate from #30 failure-audit evidence.
nonGoals: No executor, UI, CLI, finding ledger, baseline policy, Hindsight adapter, GdUnit implementation, project test implementation, target migration, issue publisher, or deployment is implemented by this contract-planning issue. No automatic test discovery or rewrite of existing project validation commands.
risks: Risk is high because this is a cross-project persisted/public contract. A false green can waive required coverage; an incompatible run-record field can make older Cezar versions drop records; shell-string semantics differ across Windows and Linux; raw paths/logs can disclose private data. Mitigate with an optional versioned manifest, argv-based new checks, optional additive persisted fields, fail-closed unknown/incomplete statuses, bounded redacted outputs, relative artifact paths, and independent cross-platform fixtures. Human plan approval is required before implementation.
dependencies: #48 audit is complete. Coordinate the legacy validation.changed/full/verify contract with open #19 and registered-target compatibility with open #39. #50 consumes this execution contract; #51 supplies the pilot adapter; #52 owns the durable finding ledger; #54 owns debt/baseline policy. #22/#30/#31 remain the sole bounded failure-audit and canonical issue-publication flow. No Hindsight integration was available for recall; no memories were queried.
suggestedWorkBreakdown: 1. Add an optional root verification block with version: 1, named checks, suites, optional capability requirements, timeouts and exclusive resource keys; leave existing validation fields untouched. 2. Define a shell-independent command descriptor using executable plus argv, project-relative cwd, explicit environment allowlist, tags/ownership metadata and bounded timeout. 3. Define versioned immutable VerificationRun and CheckRun results with required status, coverage, diagnostics, metrics, fingerprint, environment/tool versions, manifest/commit/worktree provenance and relative artifact references. 4. Specify aggregation and semantic exit codes: 0 passed, 1 required test failure, 2 incomplete/no-tests/unknown/unsupported schema, 3 infrastructure/timeout/crash, 4 cancelled; preserve the raw child exit code separately. 5. Set bounds: 256 checks/run, 3600 seconds/check, 20,000-character combined output preview/check, 200 diagnostics/check at 2,000 characters each, 128 metrics/check, 100 artifact references/run and a 1 MiB serialized result; record truncation explicitly. 6. Add valid legacy and v1 plus malformed/unsupported/empty/partial/crash/truncated fixtures and schema documentation; consume the fixture corpus in Cezar and an independent non-Cezar implementation on Windows and Linux. 7. Prove legacy adapter compatibility and document migration/rollout gates with #19/#39; keep issue publication and performance-baseline comparison in their existing work packages.
unresolvedQuestions: No schema-design question blocks this proposal. The caps above are explicit starting limits and must be reviewed against representative artifacts before implementation. The result is ready for human plan review only; it is not implementation authorization. Reconcile #19/#39 before target rollout and obtain the policy-required high-risk plan approval before #50 or any implementation begins.
